claims.statement: Best universal bounds in the literature: H <= sum_i h(Inf_i) (Keller-Mossel-Schlank arXiv:1105.2651; Han arXiv:2312.08271); H[f^{<=D}] <= K sum_{|S|<=D} |S| log(|S|+1) fhat(S)^2 + K I (Kelman-Kindler-Lifshitz-Minzer-Safra arXiv:1911.10579v2, Thm 1.3); H <= 2 aUC_parity (Arunachalam et al. arXiv:1809.09819); H <= 2(deg-1) (granularity). Classes: plateaued functions sharp constant 4 (Potapov arXiv:2609.21563); Hod lower bound 6.454784 (arXiv:1711.00762).

claims.statement: Meta-obstruction: Slote (arXiv:2608.01424) gives quantum Boolean functions (Hermitian unitaries) of Pauli degree d with exp(Theta(d^2)) equal-magnitude Pauli terms, so H/I = Theta(d). Hence any argument whose steps all remain valid for quantum Boolean functions (Parseval, hypercontractivity, LSI, KKL/Talagrand/Friedgut-type estimates, operator Booleanity A^2 = I) cannot prove FEI or any bound H <= C sum_P p_P psi(|P|) + C I with psi(d) = o(d); in particular KKLMS Thm 1.3 fails quantumly, so its proof must use classical structure. Mechanism: anticommuting labels P_l make sum_l P_l (x) B_l unitary whenever sum_l B_l^2 = I (verified for the smallest case).
claims.remaining_gap: logical statement only; does not say which classical ingredient suffices

claims.statement: For every Boolean f and nonempty S: |fhat(S)| <= 2^{|S|-1} I_S(f), where I_S(f) = sum_{T superset of S} fhat(T)^2 = E[(d_S f)^2]; equivalently p_S <= 4^{|S|-1} pi(S)^2. (d_S f takes values in 2^{1-|S|} Z because it is 2^{-|S|} times a sum of 2^{|S|} signs.)
claims.where: NOTES.md sec. 5.3 (Lemma G-key); exact integer check code/check_Gkey.py
claims.remaining_gap: none; novelty unverified (elementary)

claims.statement: Theorem G: for every Boolean f, H(f) <= 2(I(f) - Var(f)) + 2 U(f) - (1-Var) log2(1/(1-Var)) <= 2 I(f) + 2 U(f), where U(f) = sum_S p_S log2(pi(S)/p_S) and pi(S) = sum_{T superset of S} p_T. Also U <= H, so FEI holds iff sup U/I < infinity, with C_FEI <= 2 + 2 sup(U/I) and sup(U/I) >= (6.4548-2)/2 by Hod.
claims.remaining_gap: the FEI-equivalent statement U <= K I is open

claims.statement: Theorem G is tight: equality for all addressing functions tested and 2-bit bent; ratio H/(2(I-Var)+2U) -> 1 on point defects and reaches 0.986 on near-extremal read-once AND/OR formulas with H/I = 5.91 (U/I = 2.06), so on the extremal family C_FEI is governed by sup U/I.

claims.statement: Level-only universal bounds: H <= 2(I-Var) + 2H(W) + 2 sum_{k>=1} W_k log2 E[binom(|S|,k)] (W_k = P(|S| = k); equal to Theorem G for symmetric functions); and, tensor-stable, H <= 2(I-Var) + 2 inf_{lambda>0} [log2 E(1+lambda)^{|S|} - I log2 lambda] (lambda = 1: H <= 2I + 2 log2 E 2^{|S|}).
claims.remaining_gap: both lose on heavy |S|-tails (G1 not tensor-stable; G2 weak for majority); incomparable with KKLMS

claims.statement: For read-once compositions f = g(h_1..h_k) with independent inner functions: U(f) = U(P_g^mu) + sum_j P(j in J) U(q_j), parallel to H(f) = H(P_g^mu) + sum_j P(j in J) H(q_j), I(f) = sum_j P(j in J) E_{q_j}|T|.
claims.remaining_gap: none

claims.statement: Exact restriction identity: Delta_i U = sum_{T not containing i} m_T [ s_T log2(r_T/s_T) + (1-s_T) log2(1/(1-s_T)) + D2((1+eta_T)/2 || (1+x_T)/2) ], with m_T = fhat(T)^2 + fhat(T+i)^2, s_T = fhat(T+i)^2/m_T, r_T = pi(T+i)/pi(T), eta_T and x_T the restriction asymmetries of the T-coefficient and of the T-upper-set mass. Equivalently Delta_i U = B_i - Gamma_i + K_i with K_i = U(law of S minus i) - avg U(f_{i,+-}) >= 0. Chain rules for any law: H = sum_k B_{i_k}(P_k), U = sum_k [B - Gamma]_{i_k}(P_k), H - U = sum_k Gamma_{i_k}(P_k) along any marginalisation order.
claims.where: NOTES.md sec. 5.1 and 5.3; verified to 1e-10 in code/dU_exact.py and exactly in code/chainU.py
claims.remaining_gap: none

best_next_step: Prove the FEI-equivalent statement U(f) <= K I(f) through the restriction identity of sec. 5.1: the local logarithm is already refunded, so it suffices to bound the KL asymmetry term K_i = U(law of S minus i) - avg U(f_{i,+-}) (the concavity gap of U under merging the two restriction spectra) in aggregate, e.g. sum_i K_i <= a I + b U with b < 1 minus the L_down - Gamma part. Since U-statements are not contradicted by the quantum counterexample, hypercontractive or log-Sobolev arguments on the upper-set masses pi(S) = E[(d_S f)^2] are admissible here, while the classical-only input is already spent in Lemma G-key.
